release_notes:
Verify password resets with an emailed code, and stop the duplicated greeting

A reset used to generate a new password immediately and email it, so anyone who knew a username could change that customer's password at will, locking them out until they read the email and leaving a plaintext password in their inbox.

Reset is now two steps, mirroring the logged-in change-password flow: identifying the account emails a 6-digit code and changes nothing, then the code, the new password and its confirmation are submitted together and the password is written only once the code verifies. Codes last ten minutes, allow five wrong attempts, cap resends, are compared with hash_equals and are cleared after use. The new password must meet the same strength rule, trusted devices are signed out, and a confirmation email follows. The response is identical whether or not the account exists, so the form cannot be used to test which accounts are registered.

Password emails also arrived with two greetings stacked, because the wrapper template renders Hi #NAME# from the toName argument while the body greeted as well and the literal 'Customer' was being passed. Bodies no longer greet, both flows pass the customer's name, and the fallback lives in one shared helper.
